report.summary: The single failure is a test bug, not a product bug: test_current_year_is_accepted posts year THIS_YEAR + 1 and expects 201, but the app correctly rejects any year above the current one with 422. The same suite already asserts that next-year is rejected (test_invalid_book_is_rejected, 'next-year' case), so the two tests contradict each other. Fix the test to use THIS_YEAR, which is what its name describes, and do not change the app.

causes.title: Test submits next year and expects it to be accepted
causes.explanation: test_current_year_is_accepted is named for the current year but builds its request with year=THIS_YEAR + 1. The app's validate_book only accepts 1 <= year <= date.today().year, so a next-year value is rejected with 422 every time. The app's behavior matches the rule the suite itself asserts elsewhere, so the assertion is wrong, not the app. The failure is deterministic and has nothing to do with timing.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:47-50: def test_current_year_is_accepted(api): response = api.create_book(title=unique("New"), author="Someone", year=THIS_YEAR + 1); assert response.status_code == 201
app/main.py:81-84: if book.year is not None: this_year = date.today().year; if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/api/test_books_api.py:58: ({"title": "T", "author": "A", "year": THIS_YEAR + 1}, "Year must be between") expects 422 for next year, contradicting the failing test
causes.suggested_fix: Change the year argument in tests/api/test_books_api.py:48 from THIS_YEAR + 1 to THIS_YEAR so the test checks the current-year boundary as its name says. Keep the next-year case in test_invalid_book_is_rejected as the rejection test. Optionally add a year=1 acceptance case to cover the lower bound.
